CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS 
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS analytics_events  ( id                  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY ASC AUTOINCREMENT  , event_name          TEXT NOT NULL  , sub_event_name      TEXT NOT NULL  , module              TEXT NOT NULL  , event_timestamp     NUMERIC NOT NULL  , requested_latency   NUMERIC NOT NULL  , event_tag           INTEGER NOT NULL  , applied_sample_rate INTEGER NOT NULL  , event_byte_size     INTEGER NOT NULL  , app_identity        TEXT NOT NULL  , device_identity     TEXT NOT NULL  , user_identity       TEXT NOT NULL  , event_payload       BLOB NOT NULL  , stored_timestamp    NUMERIC NOT NULL  , privacy_context     TEXT DEFAULT ''  , compression_type    INTEGER DEFAULT 0  , trace_id            TEXT DEFAULT ''  , upload_domain_type  INTEGER DEFAULT 0  );
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS analytics_uploads  ( id                  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY ASC AUTOINCREMENT  , batched_timestamp   NUMERIC NOT NULL  , is_multi_batch      INTEGER NOT NULL  , events_count        INTEGER NOT NULL  , batches_count       INTEGER NOT NULL  , upload_byte_size    INTEGER NOT NULL  , retry_count         INTEGER DEFAULT 0  , minimum_latency     NUMERIC NOT NULL  , events_in_upload    TEXT NOT NULL  , upload_payload      BLOB NOT NULL  , upload_status       INTEGER NOT NULL  , stored_timestamp    NUMERIC NOT NULL  , compression_type    INTEGER DEFAULT 0  , upload_domain_type  INTEGER DEFAULT 0  , event_timestamps_in_upload TEXT DEFAULT ''  );
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS buffer_event(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,identities_hash INTEGER,name TEXT,time_in_ms INTEGER,tags INTEGER,sample_rate INTEGER,requested_latency INTEGER,extra TEXT,extra_binary BINARY,compression_method TEXT,trace_id TEXT)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS checksum(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,checksum_hash INTEGER UNIQUE,identities_hash INTEGER,type INTEGER,checksum TEXT,timestamp INTEGER)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS claim(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,principal_subject_hash INTEGER,claim TEXT,expires_at INTEGER)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS collection_constraint(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,identities_hash INTEGER,node_type INTEGER,value INTEGER,expression_op TEXT,expression_refs TEXT,mode_bit INTEGER)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS data(      key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,      data BLOB NOT NULL,      extra BLOB,      lastaccess INT NON NULL,      insert_time INT NON NULL DEFAULT 0,      ttl INT NON NULL DEFAULT 0,      priority INT NON NULL DEFAULT 0    );    CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS la_index ON data(lastaccess);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS event_config(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,event_config_hash INTEGER UNIQUE,identities_hash INTEGER,event_name TEXT,sampling_rate INTEGER,collection_constraint_ref INTEGER,is_deidentified INTEGER)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS origin(key TEXT NOT NULL,origin TEXT NOT NULL,get_count INTEGER NOT NULL,insert_count INTEGER NOT NULL,remove_count INTEGER NOT NULL,PRIMARY KEY(key,origin))
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS store_metadata(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,val TEXT)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS upload(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,request_data BINARY,num_events INTEGER,is_compressed INTEGER,compression_method TEXT)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS utilization(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,cache_name TEXT NOT NULL,session_key TEXT NOT NULL,cache_key TEXT NOT NULL,item_size INTEGER,action_count INTEGER NOT NULL,get_count INTEGER NOT NULL,hit_count INTEGER NOT NULL,insert_count INTEGER NOT NULL,remove_count INTEGER NOT NULL,remove_unknown INTEGER NOT NULL,remove_user INTEGER NOT NULL,remove_eviction INTEGER NOT NULL,remove_stale INTEGER NOT NULL,refetch_count INTEGER NOT NULL,refresh_count INTEGER NOT NULL,tracking_start_time INTEGER NOT NULL,last_known INTEGER NOT NULL,had_known INTEGER NOT NULL,metadata TEXT)

Saves to the default account's default folder unless folder names a unique folder; shared folders are not supported. Create calendar event

Items: title, start_date, end_date or duration (ISO 8601); optional calendar_id (device default), location, notes, is_all_day, availability, timezone, reminder_minutes, rrule or recurrence_frequency/interval/days_of_week/count/end_date. Dates need a UTC offset, or yyyy-MM-dd for UTC midnight; end must follow start (all-day ends are exclusive). Retry only failed entries; successes are kept.

Rows with accessibility=false are windows the selected app opened for your earlier input but doesn't list for Accessibility. activate with window_id set to a row's surface_id selects it from its screenshot only: clicks at points of its image work there, and typing into a field you clicked.
Rows with on_current_space=false are windows on another Space (full_screen=true: in full screen on a Space of their own). activate can select one by its window_id. Element actions then reach it there without switching Spaces, and key, and type without element_number, go to the app's keyboard window there when that is the selected window or one an action opened. Pointer input needs it on the user's Space, and computer control doesn't switch Spaces on its own: ask the user first. If a window can't be selected, ask the user to switch to it themselves or exit full screen.
Rows with stage_manager=side_strip are windows in Stage Manager's side strip, off the stage. activate can select one, and element actions then reach it there without bringing it to the stage. Pointer and key input need it on the stage, and computer control doesn't move it there on its own: ask the user first.

SSL - * Early data has been received as part of an on-going handshake. This error code can be returned only on server side if and only if early data has been enabled by means of the mbedtls_ssl_conf_early_data() API. This error code can then be returned by mbedtls_ssl_handshake(), mbedtls_ssl_handshake_step(), mbedtls_ssl_read() or mbedtls_ssl_write() if early data has been received as part of the handshake sequence they triggered. SSL - Attempt to verify a certificate without an expected hostname. This is usually insecure.  In TLS clients, when a client authenticates a server through its certificate, the client normally checks three things: - the certificate chain must be valid; - the chain must start from a trusted CA; - the certificate must cover the server name that is expected by the client.  Omitting any of these checks is generally insecure, and can allow a malicious server to impersonate a legitimate server.  The third check may be safely skipped in some unusual scenarios, such as networks where eavesdropping is a risk but not active attacks, or a private PKI where the client equally trusts all servers that are accredited by the root CA.  You should call mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname() with the expected server name before starting a TLS handshake on a client (unless the client is set up to only use PSK-based authentication, which does not rely on the host name). If you have determined that server name verification is not required for security in your scenario, call mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname() with \p NULL as the server name.  This error is raised if all of the following conditions are met:  - A TLS client is configured with the authentication mode #MBEDTLS_SSL_VERIFY_REQUIRED (default). - Certificate authentication is enabled. - The client does not call mbedtls_ssl_set_hostname(). - The configuration option #MBEDTLS_SSL_CLI_ALLOW_WEAK_CERTIFICATE_VERIFICATION_WITHOUT_HOSTNAME is not enabled

WPS OffiH
WPS Office's document tabs aren't Accessibility controls, so click_element can't press them. Switch documents with keys instead: key ctrl+shift+tab moves one tab to the left and key ctrl+tab one tab to the right. Before key cmd+w, confirm from the window's title or the capture that the current document is the one to close, and afterwards switch back to the document the user was on. Its "View document tabs" button only shows the tabs' order: close that list with key escape, and don't press return in it.
WPS draws its slides itself, so its text boxes don't show as text fields and typed letters would run its shortcuts. No key input was sent.
WPS draws its slides itself: a paste goes into a text box only after a click has put the cursor in it; otherwise WPS makes a new text box on the slide. Nothing was pasted and the clipboard is unchanged.

[[stitchable]] float4 applyGainMap( coreimage::sample_t sdr, coreimage::sample_t gm, float max_display_boost, float gain_map_min, float gain_map_max, float gamma, float offset_sdr, float offset_hdr, float hdr_capacity_min, float hdr_capacity_max ) { sdr = clamp(sdr, 0.0, 1.0); float3 recovery = clamp(gm.rgb, 0.0, 1.0); float3 log_recovery = pow(recovery, 1.0 / gamma); float3 unclamped_weight_factor = (log2(max_display_boost) - hdr_capacity_min) / (hdr_capacity_max - hdr_capacity_min); float3 weight_factor = clamp(unclamped_weight_factor, 0.0, 1.0); float3 log_boost = gain_map_min * (1.0 - log_recovery) + gain_map_max * log_recovery; float3 hdr = (sdr.rgb + offset_sdr) * exp2(log_boost * weight_factor) - offset_hdr; return float4(hdr, sdr.a); }

`internal
`is_from_me: true` means the USER wrote it; then `sender_handle` is the other party and there is no `sender_name`. `sender_name` appears only on a received message whose handle matched the user's contacts. `participant_names` lists everyone in the THREAD, never a given message's sender; `chat_display_name` is a title the user chose. A received message with no `sender_name` is from someone unidentified: use the handle or ask the user, and NEVER infer the sender from the text, the thread name, or the other participants. Handles in `reactions` and `reply_context` are never named; look them up in `participant_names` rather than treating them as unidentified. Each `reply_context` has its own `is_from_me` (true: the USER wrote the quote, and its handle is not the author); never take the quote's author from the message containing it.
